new_statements.quote: ACCENTUATION. — Les différents accents : ouvert, fermé, long, bref, nasal, tonique qui se divise lui-même en accent tonique proprement dit, en accent de hauteur, jouent le plus grand rôle dans l'intelligibilité de cette langue. Il importe donc de les bien observer et de ne pas les confondre. ACCENT TONIQUE. — L'accent tonique consiste dans un ' coup de voix ' sans élévation sensible du ton. La syllabe qui le porte est prononcée avec plus d'intensité ou d'effort. Il se trouve ordinairement sur la première syllabe non affectée du signe de brièveté. ACCENT DE HAUTEUR. — L'accent de hauteur consiste dans une élévation du ton, soit sur un mot monosyllabique, soit sur une ou plusieurs syllabes du même mot.
new_statements.translation: ACCENTUATION. — The various accents: open, close, long, short, nasal, tonic (which itself divides into the tonic accent proper and the pitch accent) play the greatest role in the intelligibility of this language. It is therefore important to observe them well and not to confuse them. TONIC ACCENT. — The tonic accent consists in a 'burst of voice' without noticeable raising of pitch. The syllable that bears it is pronounced with more intensity or effort. It is ordinarily found on the first syllable not marked with the sign of shortness. PITCH ACCENT. — The pitch accent consists in a raising of the pitch, either on a monosyllabic word or on one or several syllables of the same word.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Intensity stress (kept distinct by the author from pitch/tone, which is marked with an acute) ordinarily falls on the first syllable of the word; if the first syllable carries the breve (short-vowel) sign, stress goes to the next syllable not so marked. Pitch ('accent de hauteur') is independent and may sit on any one or several syllables, i.e. lexical tone.
new_statements.exceptions: 'ordinairement' (ordinarily); syllables marked short (breve) do not take the stress, which then falls on the first non-short syllable. No lexical exceptions listed.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement in a missionary grammar covering Gmbwaga (= Ngbaka Ma'bo), Gbanziri and Monjombo jointly as 'three dialects of one language'; impressionistic, pre-phonemic (1911). The language is tonal (Thomas 1963/1970: three level tones plus contour tones); Calloc'h's 'accent de hauteur' corresponds to tone. The modern reference grammar (Thomas 1963) was not accessible and may treat accent differently.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted source (Calloc'h 1911) describes 'Gmbwaga' as spoken on the Ubangi river near the Bangui Catholic mission; Gmbwaga = Ngbaka Ma'bo (Bwaka/Gbwaka, ngba1284). Calloc'h treats Gmbwaga, Gbanziri (Glottolog gban1258 Gbanziri-Boraka) and Monjombo (monz1249 Monzombo) as 'trois dialectes d'une meme langue' and the grammar section, including the accent paragraph, is written for all three jointly (examples numbered 1 = Gmbwaga, 2 = Gbanziri, 3 = Monjombo). The modern reference description, Thomas 1963, is of the Bokanga village variety (Lobaye, CAR) of Ngbaka Ma'bo. NB: Glottolog's descriptive list for ngba1284 includes Henrix, van den Eynde & Meeuwis 2007 'Description grammaticale de la langue Ngbaka' (Lincom), which describes Ngbaka Minagende (nga, ngba1285, a Gbaya-Manza-Ngbaka language), not Ngbaka Ma'bo; likewise GrandEury 1991 is on Ngbaka Minagende.

tone_statements.citation: Roulon, Paulette. 1972. Etude du francais et du sango parles par les Ngbaka-Ma'Bo (Republique Centrafricaine). Ethnies (Collection IDERIC, Nice) 2: 133-165 (sec. 2.3.3 'Tons et prosodie', pp. 145-146).
tone_statements.quote: 2.3.3. Tons et prosodie. Le ngbaka et le sango sont des langues à tons. Ces derniers n'affectent que les voyelles. Les tons ont une fonction distinctive dans ces langues au même titre que l'aperture ou la nasalité. Le ngbaka et le sango présentent un système de tons à trois niveaux : haut moyen et bas[ˇ], qui par leurs combinaisons donnent un certain nombre de tons mélodiques. Ainsi, en ngbaka on a, outre les tons ponctuels [...], les tons mélodiques suivants [five contour marks, garbled in the scanned: /\ , / , \- , V\ , V].
tone_statements.translation: 2.3.3. Tones and prosody. Ngbaka and Sango are tone languages. The tones affect only the vowels. Tones have a distinctive function in these languages in the same way as aperture or nasality. Ngbaka and Sango have a tone system with three levels: high, mid and low, which through their combinations yield a number of melodic (contour) tones. Thus in Ngbaka one has, besides the level tones, the following melodic tones [five contours].
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: Three level ('ponctuel') tones H, M, L on vowels (vowel = tone-bearing unit), plus five contour ('melodic') tones formed by combining the levels; tone lexically distinctive; nothing on stress, downstep or floating tones (inventory follows Thomas 1963).

tone.quote: The material is extremely accurately transcribed, with great attention to the tonal factor. Initial confusion might perhaps be caused to the reader by the author's use of double vowels to accommodate moving tone values on what are really single vowels. Thus mā mid tone, mà low tone, but máā high-mid, māá mid-high, māà mid-low, màā low-mid (which other toneticians, with more amenable printers at their service, might prefer to write … ). … Since vowel length is not a significant factor, no harm is done, and diphthongs of the type sīà, tíā satisfactorily taken care of.
tone.locator: p. 367, first paragraph of the review
tone.summary: One-page review of Thomas 1963: praises the tone transcription and illustrates mid, low and high marks plus moving tones (high-mid, mid-high, mid-low, low-mid) on doubled vowels; states no inventory.

tone.quote: Par contre, la langue ngbaka mabo elle-même semble être homogène. Les interviewés ont fait une distinction entre les Ngbaka qui habitent dans la forêt et ceux qui habitent dans la savane. … Ces répartitions n’entrainent pas de distinction dialectale. Les locuteurs ont insisté pour affirmer que l’intercompréhension entre eux est parfaite. Les différences sont soit des différences de tonalité, soit des variations de vocabulaire, etc., mais elles sont légères.
tone.locator: p. 5, §3.1.1 Étendue et homogénéité (last paragraph before §3.1.2)
tone.translation: By contrast, the Ngbaka Mabo language itself seems to be homogeneous. The interviewees distinguished the Ngbaka who live in the forest from those who live in the savanna. … These divisions do not entail any dialect distinction. The speakers insisted that mutual comprehension among them is perfect. The differences are either differences of tonality or variations of vocabulary, etc., but they are slight.
tone.summary: Sociolinguistic survey only: speakers report slight 'differences of tonality' between sub-groups; no tone inventory or analysis given; refers to Thomas 1963 for the description.
